t.5.30.2: But she, the beautiful Maithilī, seeing the best of monkeys standing near her humbly, thought, "This is a dream."
t.5.30.1: Then, seeing him hidden among the branches, she, her mind shaken, beheld there the monkey, modest and sweet of speech.
t.5.30.3: On merely beholding him, Sītā fell utterly senseless and became as one whose life had departed; and after a long while, regaining consciousness, the large-eyed one began to reflect.
t.5.30.4: Today I have seen this ill-omened dream, a monkey, which the whole body of śāstras declares forbidden. May all be well with Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa, and likewise with my father, King Janaka.
t.5.30.5: This is not even a dream, for there is no sleep for me, tormented as I am by sorrow and grief. Nor is there any happiness for me, since I am bereft of him whose face is like the full moon.
t.5.30.6: For today, tormented by love for him, my whole being fixed on him, and thinking of him alone without ceasing, I see him just so, and just so I hear him.
t.5.30.7: I think this may be only a wish of my mind, yet I also reason it through with my intellect: what could be its cause? For a wish has no form, and yet this one, whose form is clearly manifest, speaks to me.
t.5.30.8: Salutation to Vācaspati together with the wielder of the thunderbolt, to Svayambhū, and to Hutāśana! Whatever this forest-dweller has spoken here before me, may it be just so and not otherwise.
